objective: Telling apart an issue, a risk, an assumption, and a constraint, and reviewing a project scope statement for gaps

sources.cite: PMI, Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) Examination Content Outline, 2023 Exam Update: Fundamentals and Core Concepts 36%, Predictive Plan-Based Methodologies 17%, Agile Frameworks/Methodologies 20%, Business Analysis Frameworks 27%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a university. Relevant text: Domain 1 Task 5 'Demonstrate an understanding of common problem-solving tools and techniques' ('Evaluate the effectiveness of a meeting'; 'Explain the purpose of focus groups, standup meetings, brainstorming, etc.'); Domain 2 Task 2 ('Apply critical path methods'; 'Calculate schedule variance') and Task 3 ('Calculate cost and schedule variances'). The objective wording here is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's sprint-status-meeting-daily-scrum-capm (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are a project coordinator on the fictional Elm Street community center renovation. Your project manager asks you to tidy the logs and review the scope statement before the sponsor meeting.
handover: The 'risk log' mixes things that have happened with things that might.
The scope statement was written in one afternoon.
howItWorks: The dashboard shows the commitments, the work items, the risks and issues, the people's support and the milestones.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each status meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: rain soaks the hall's new drywall; the leaking roof had waited in the risk log.
Week 3: asbestos is confirmed; contingency is already spent on the kitchen and work stops for six weeks.
Week 4: the expanded scope prices at 1.2 million dollars; the board refuses and the project pauses.

sortPrompt.title: Everything in one log
sortPrompt.context: Events, possibilities, beliefs and limits are mixed.

choices.label: Move 'roof leaking now' to the issue log with an owner, keep 'possible asbestos' as a risk, record the March grant as an assumption to validate, and the budget cap as a constraint

effects.log: Each item is in the right place with an owner.

choices.feedback: An issue has happened, a risk might, an assumption is believed true without proof, and a constraint is a fixed limit.

choices.label: Rename the log 'RAID' and leave the items mixed
choices.feedback: The leaking roof still waits as if it might happen.

choices.label: Treat everything as a risk and schedule a review next month
choices.feedback: The roof is already leaking; treating it as a risk delays action.

assumePrompt.title: An assumption under strain
assumePrompt.context: The funder says the grant may come in May, not March.

choices.label: Confirm the date with the funder, record the assumption as invalid, and add a risk with a response (stage the kitchen work after May)

effects.log: The plan reflects a May grant.

choices.feedback: Assumptions are validated; when one fails, it becomes a risk or an issue with a response.

choices.label: Keep the March assumption and hope
choices.feedback: The plan rests on a date the funder doubts.

choices.label: Start the kitchen in March using the contingency, expecting the grant to repay it
choices.feedback: If the grant slips, contingency is gone before the asbestos risk is known.

gapsPrompt.title: A thin scope statement
gapsPrompt.context: No acceptance criteria, no exclusions, a vague kitchen.

choices.label: Add acceptance criteria for each deliverable, list exclusions (parking lot, furniture), and define the kitchen's scope with the sponsor

effects.log: The sponsor approves the revised statement.

choices.feedback: A scope statement needs deliverables, acceptance criteria and exclusions; gaps become disputes later.

choices.label: Leave it; details will come up during the work
choices.feedback: Every unstated expectation becomes a change request or a dispute.

choices.label: Add everything stakeholders mention, including the parking lot
choices.feedback: The cap of 900 thousand dollars cannot cover it.

reflection.question: Write the project log summary for the sponsor meeting.

parts.label: Logs
parts.criteria: Roof as an issue; asbestos as a risk; grant as an assumption now invalid; budget cap as a constraint.
parts.modelAnswer: The leaking roof is an issue being fixed; asbestos is a risk; the March grant was an assumption, now a May risk with a response; the 900 thousand dollar cap is a constraint.

parts.label: Scope
parts.criteria: Acceptance criteria, exclusions and kitchen detail added.

Separate the four kinds and give each an owner.
Validate the assumption and add a risk with a response.
Add criteria, exclusions and missing detail.

sortHarm.headline: Act on issues
sortHarm.body: Issues need action now; risks need responses.

target.headline: Good: a project the sponsor can follow

scoring.modelReasoning: An issue has happened; a risk might happen; an assumption is believed true and must be validated; a constraint is a fixed limit. Separate them so each gets the right handling. A scope statement needs acceptance criteria and exclusions, closed within the project's constraints.
